title: One vehicle access point per lot
text: Vehicle access points are limited to one per lot (refer Figure 3.7a) except where: i. an existing dwelling is being retained that has an established access point that is not able to serve the other dwellings; ii. dwellings front the street and access is not available from a communal street or rear right-of-way; or iii. the lot frontage exceeds 40m, two vehicle access points are permitted.

exceptions.label: (i) retained dwelling with an established access point
(ii) dwellings front the street and no communal street or rear ROW access
(iii) lot frontage exceeds 40 m: two access points

replaces.note: register C4P1-109 says unchanged; ch3 register found Part B had no one-access limit, which would make R10-R25 tightened

notes: diverges: from ch3 C3.7.2, coding widened. Chapter 4 Part 1 C3.7.2 (p39) has no 'In areas R40 and above' qualifier, so the one-access-per-lot limit applies at R10-R60 (Chapter 3: R40+). Exceptions unchanged: (i) and (ii) are tested only on retention and on the absence of a communal street or rear ROW ('not able to serve the other dwellings' and 'dwellings front the street' have no facts). proposal.retained_dwelling is used although this chapter has no retained-dwelling element.

verified.note: Wording confirmed; no 'In areas R40 and above' qualifier on this page, so R10-R60 is right. Exceptions (i) and (ii) state no effect; (i) 'not able to serve the other dwellings' and (ii) 'dwellings front the street' have no facts. Encoded as not applicable on retention / absence of a communal street or rear ROW.
